description: P2/P3 features — vector memory (pgvector), Sigma rule auto-generation, finding dedup logic, HTML/PDF report export, and resource library. These five span new Go packages and new API endpoints. They are independent of FEAT-001/002/003 except that the resource library's list_resources/read_resource tools follow the same tool registration pattern as finding_retests tools. Implement in order: dedup first (simplest DB change), then resource library, then HTML/PDF report, then Sigma, then vector memory.
steps: SECTION A: Finding Dedup Logic Enhancement

A1. db/findings.go: Add function `FindDuplicateFinding(taskID int64, vulnclass, url, paramName string) (*DBFinding, error)` that queries: `SELECT <findingSelectCols> FROM findings f LEFT JOIN tasks t ON f.task_id=t.id WHERE f.task_id=$1 AND f.vulnclass=$2 AND f.summary ILIKE '%' || $3 || '%' LIMIT 1` — a conservative URL+vulnclass match. Return nil if no match.

A2. server/finding_workflow.go: In the report_finding tool handler, before calling RecordFinding, extract the target URL from the evidence/summary fields. Call FindDuplicateFinding. If a duplicate is found, return the existing finding's ID and node_id to the agent (JSON: {finding_id, finding_node_id, duplicate: true, message: '중복 취약점이 이미 등록되어 있습니다. 기존 ID를 사용하세요.'}) without creating a new finding. If not duplicate, proceed normally.

A3. agent/finding_workflow.go: In findingWorkflowTools(), add a note to the report_finding tool description explaining the dedup behavior: when a duplicate is returned, the agent should use the existing ID for traffic binding and report updating rather than creating another finding.
SECTION B: Resource Library

B1. db/schema.sql: Add a new table: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS resources (id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, filename TEXT NOT NULL, size BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, mime_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', description TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()); CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_resources_name ON resources(name);`

B2. db/resources.go (new file): Add CRUD functions: ListResources() ([]*Resource, error), GetResource(id int64) (*Resource, error), CreateResource(name, filename, mimeType, description string, size int64) (int64, error), DeleteResource(id int64) error. The Resource struct mirrors the table columns.

B3. server/resources.go (new file): Implement handlers: listResources (GET /api/resources), uploadResource (POST /api/resources, multipart form, save file to data/resources/<uuid>_<filename>), getResourceMeta (GET /api/resources/{id}), deleteResource (DELETE /api/resources/{id}, removes file + DB row). Create data/resources/ directory on first upload if not exists. Add Korean error constants for file too large (max 50MB), unsupported type.

B4. server/server.go: Register routes: `mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/resources", s.listResources)`, `mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/resources", s.uploadResource)`, `mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/resources/{id}", s.getResourceMeta)`, `mux.HandleFunc("DELETE /api/resources/{id}", s.deleteResource)`, `mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/resources/{id}/download", s.downloadResource)`.

B5. agent/tools.go or agent/toolcatalog.go: Add two agent tools `list_resources` (no params, returns JSON list of resources) and `read_resource` (param: id int64, returns file content as base64 for binary or text for text files, capped at 1MB). Register them in the tool catalog following the pattern of other read-only tools. These are wired via the server's tool registration mechanism (see server/finding_retests.go seedFindingRetester pattern — use SeedTool).
SECTION C: HTML/PDF Report Export

C1. report/html.go (new file): Add HTMLReport(in Input) string function that renders a complete HTML document using Go's html/template package. The template should include: a styled header (task name, generated date), executive summary table (finding counts by severity), a findings section with severity badges, CVSS score (from new field), evidence/PoC in pre blocks. The template string is embedded inline as a Go const.

C2. server/server.go: Register `mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/tasks/{id}/report", s.taskReport)`. Implement taskReport in server/task_report.go (new file). The handler reads query param `format` (html, pdf, md — default md). For 'md': existing Markdown logic (call report.Markdown). For 'html': call report.HTMLReport, return Content-Type text/html. For 'pdf': call report.HTMLReport, then run a system command `wkhtmltopdf - output.pdf` piped via os/exec, return Content-Type application/pdf. If wkhtmltopdf is not available, return 501 with Korean error '시스템에 PDF 변환 도구(wkhtmltopdf)가 설치되지 않았습니다'.

C3. server/task_report.go: The handler fetches findings via s.m.pg.ListFindingsForTask(taskID) and task details, builds report.Input, then renders per format. Set Content-Disposition header to attachment for pdf/html downloads.
SECTION D: Sigma Rule Auto-generation

D1. agent/finding_workflow.go: After a finding is successfully recorded (in the existing finding reporter trigger path), if the finding has traffic_refs, generate a Sigma rule. Add a function generateSigmaRule(finding *db.DBFinding, trafficSummary string) string that returns a YAML Sigma rule string using a Go text/template. The rule template: title (finding name), description, logsource (category: webserver), detection (keywords from URL/payload extracted from evidence), falsepositives, level (map severity to sigma level: critical→critical, high→high, medium→medium, low→low).

D2. server/finding_workflow.go (or report/sigma.go, new file): The generateSigmaRule function extracts: target URL path, any payload keywords from evidence (look for patterns like `'`, `<script`, `../`, `; `, `UNION SELECT` in evidence text), creates a Sigma rule. Save the rule to `detections/sigma/<vulnclass>_<finding_id>.yml` using os.WriteFile, creating the directory if needed.
D3. db/schema.sql: No schema change needed — Sigma rules are saved as files.
SECTION E: Vector Memory (pgvector)

E1. db/schema.sql: Add pgvector extension setup (idempotent): `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;`. Add embeddings table: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS embeddings (id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, task_id BIGINT REFERENCES tasks(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, content_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'finding', content_id BIGINT, text_summary TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', embedding vector(1536), created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()); CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_embeddings_task ON embeddings(task_id); CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_embeddings_vector ON embeddings USING ivfflat(embedding vector_cosine_ops) WITH (lists=100);`

E2. memory/memory.go (new package): Create package memory with module path github.com/Autumn-27/artex/memory. Implement: type Store struct { pg *db.DB; llmProv llm.Provider; model string }. func New(pg *db.DB, llmProv llm.Provider, embeddingModel string) *Store. func (s *Store) StoreExperience(ctx context.Context, taskID int64, contentType, text string, contentID int64) error — calls the LLM provider's embeddings endpoint (POST /v1/embeddings with model and input), stores the returned vector in the embeddings table. func (s *Store) SearchSimilar(ctx context.Context, queryText string, limit int) ([]EmbeddingResult, error) — embeds queryText then queries `SELECT task_id, content_type, text_summary, 1 - (embedding <=> $1) AS similarity FROM embeddings ORDER BY embedding <=> $1 LIMIT $2`.

E3. memory/memory.go: The embeddings API call: since the LLM provider interface (llm.Provider) is for chat completions, make a direct HTTP POST to the base_url + /embeddings endpoint. Use the config.APIKey and model from the Store. Parse the response's data[0].embedding float64 array. Handle errors gracefully — if embeddings fail, log and return nil (never break the main flow).

E4. server/manager.go or server/server.go: Wire the memory.Store — create it in Server.New() or Manager, store as s.memory *memory.Store. Call s.memory.StoreExperience() after a finding is recorded (hook into the finding recorder path). Call s.memory.SearchSimilar() at worker start and inject results as a hint into the worker's initial context (add to the worker prompt via a new field in WorkerVars).

E5. go.mod: Add pgvector Go client. The pgvector Go package is `github.com/pgvector/pgvector-go` — add it via `go get github.com/pgvector/pgvector-go@latest`. Use it only for the vector column type encoding/decoding in memory/memory.go. Alternatively, encode the vector as a PostgreSQL-compatible text literal `[0.1,0.2,...]::vector` using fmt.Sprintf to avoid adding a dependency — prefer this approach to keep go.mod clean.
acceptance_criteria: go test ./... passes all existing non-DB tests.
POST /api/resources (multipart) stores file and DB record.
GET /api/tasks/{id}/report?format=html returns a complete HTML document.
detections/sigma/ directory is created if it doesn't exist.
generateSigmaRule produces valid YAML with title/logsource/detection keys.
embeddings table is in schema.sql with vector column.
Dedup: a second report_finding call with same vulnclass+summary returns {duplicate: true} without creating a new DB row.
verification: python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('detections/sigma/test.yml'))" on a generated rule — valid YAML
